title: structured-output: constrained decoding - tokenizer unicode/regex fallbacks and CFG improvements
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes:
- Improved constrained decoding backends with Unicode-aware tokenizer fallbacks
- Added regex-fallback engine for cases where tokenizer-based CFG constraints fail
- Fixed several tokenizer edge-cases causing invalid structured outputs
- Backwards-compatible; no API changes
description:
Motivation:
Applications using structured-output (CFG/regex constrained decoding) hit a class of failures when tokenization slices UTF-8 multi-codepoint graphemes in ways that break regex matching or CFG boundary detection. This causes either invalid structured outputs or decoder hangs while attempting to reconcile constraints.

This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) a tokenizer-aware Unicode fallback path that tries safe-granularity tokenization boundaries before emitting tokens to the constraint checkers; and 2) a lightweight regex-fallback decoding backend that runs a byte/char-level regex matcher when tokenizer-based constraint checks cannot be reliably applied (e.g., mixed-language inputs, emoji sequences, invisible joiners).

High-level changes:
- Add tokenizer_helpers.unicode_safe_segment() that returns candidate segment boundaries for constraint checks (tries grapheme cluster, codepoint, and token offsets).
- Add regex_fallbacks.py: a secondary constrained-decoding backend used only when primary tokenizer-based checks fail to match or would cause ambiguity.
- Update constrained_decoder.py to prefer tokenizer checks but to use regex-fallback for flagged inputs (with feature flag and telemetry).
- Expand unit/integration tests to include multilingual and emoji-heavy inputs, and add fuzz tests for tokenizer-regex interop.

Compatibility/rollout plan:
- Feature gated: rollout to 10% production traffic for hosted API, monitor structured-output success rate and latency.
- Fallback only: default behavior unchanged for most inputs; the regex-backend is only used when heuristics detect tokenizer-constraint mismatch or when enabled via explicit config.
- No user-visible API changes.

Testing notes:
- Added focused tests for unicode grapheme clusters, zero-width joiners, surrogate pairs, and combining marks.
- Reran structured-output e2e across our OpenAI-compat layer to confirm parity with previous behavior except where bugfixes change outputs (recorded in release notes).

Related: ENG-4921 (constraint robustness), ENG-5010 (tokenizer edgecases), see also PRs pr-62789 and pr-61234 for prior tokenizer-regex work.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for tokenizer helpers
- [x] Integration tests for constrained decoder backends
- [x] Performance microbenchmarks run (no >3% median token latency regression)

+++ b/redwood/serving/decoding/constrained_decoder.py
@@ -120,6 +120,22 @@
-    # previous tokenizer-only constraint check
+    # try tokenizer-based constraint checks first
+    try:
+        segments = tokenizer_helpers.unicode_safe_segment(prompt, tokenizer)
+        if constraint_engine.check_with_tokens(segments):
+            return emit_with_token_checks(segments)
+    except TokenizerAmbiguityError:
+        # fallthrough to regex backend
+        pass
+    # fallback: regex-based constraint checker
+    return regex_fallbacks.decode_with_regex(prompt, constraints)
review_conversation: Priya Nair: Nice improvement to robustness. Two concerns: (1) telemetry label cardinality when we emit fallback reasons, (2) need to ensure fallback path does not elevate worst-case latency. Can we add a rate-limited histogram?
Maya Thompson: Added a rate-limited histogram (structured_output_fallback_rate) and a labelled histogram for fallback_reason with cardinality capped to known buckets. See telemetry/metrics change.

Liam O'Connor: Integration tests look good. One nit: please prefer explicit feature-flag name 'constrained_decoding_regex_fallback' in flags config. Also add a short note in release docs about potential output diffs when fallback is used.
Maya Thompson: Renamed flag and added release note about diffs. Thx.

Diego Ramirez: Observed a flaky e2e failure on streaming/stability/test_stream_timeout in initial run — looks unrelated but worth validating memory usage when regex backend is active. Can we add a smoke memory test?
Maya Thompson: Added a lightweight memory smoke test in perf-canary that runs regex fallback on 1000 small prompts. Memory usage delta is <2% in our canary runs.
